summary: The project is an interactive Earth-system trend-analysis toolkit built around NASA Giovanni area-averaged CSV time series for three regions: the Third Pole, the boreal fire belt, and the Great Barrier Reef. app.py is the Streamlit front end. It embeds a self-contained D3/Plotly globe component where users spin the Earth, click glowing regions, and open panels showing variable-by-variable trend results. backend.py does all data loading and statistics: it recognises Giovanni variables from CSV headers, masks fill values, converts units, builds monthly series, removes the seasonal cycle, and computes least-squares trends, autocorrelation-adjusted confidence intervals and t-tests, Mann-Kendall tests, Sen’s slopes, seasonal Mann-Kendall, Hamed-Rao corrections, Pettitt change points, extreme-year robustness checks, heat-stress proxies, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR corrections. All slider-window statistics are precomputed so the front end responds instantly. The app also provides a results table and CSV download. It also flags short records, product-coverage gaps, misleading boxes, model-data caveats, and satellite artefacts, and interactively lets users adjust time windows. boreal_fire_trends.py is a standalone command-line/plotting companion for Canada and Russia that performs similar seasonal, fire-season, change-point, robustness, and FDR analyses and produces matplotlib outputs.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS - EARTH SCIENCE TREND DETECTIVE

WHAT IT DOES / HOW IT WORKS

Earth Science Trend Detective converts raw NASA GIOVANNI area-averaged monthly CSV downloads into fully tested, statistically rigorous trend analyses.

Pipeline:

1. Parse - Read each Giovanni CSV, extract the metadata header (Title, User Bounding Box, Data Bounding Box, Fill Value, Reproduce-URL), and mask fill values (1e15, -9999).

2. Normalize - Aggregate daily records to monthly means weighted by month length; snap mid-month stamps (e.g. OCO-2 CO2) to month-start. Convert units to physical values (ppb, ppm, mg/m2, degC, fraction). Reject values outside plausible ranges per variable.

3. Classify region - Map the User Bounding Box to a named sector automatically: Northern Band (48-70 N, all longitudes), Third Pole (65-105 E / 25-50 N), Boreal Canada, or Boreal Russia.

4. Test - For every variable, run:

- Seasonal Mann-Kendall (Hirsch-Slack) with tie and Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction

- Sen's slope with 95% confidence interval

- Pettitt step-change test on the annual mean

- Drop-extreme-year robustness check (remove the largest year, re-test)

- Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across all variables and tests together

5. Interpret - Render each result as a plain-English sentence: "Aerosol optical depth rose by +0.0008 AOD/decade (95% CI -0.002 to +0.004). Mann-Kendall p = 0.61 -> not significant after FDR."

Three interfaces share one engine:

- Streamlit dashboard (app.py): per-file tabs with anomaly-trend plots, monthly MK heatmaps, seasonal panels, statistics tables, Pettitt warnings, and drop-extreme-year notes.

- Globe Explorer (globe_explorer.py): rotating 3-D Earth; click a sector to open a flat regional map plus a variable-impact panel ranking drivers by Kendall tau, Spearman rho, Pearson r, lagged correlation (-6 to +6 months), and standardised beta against the sector's master trend.

- CLI batch tools (boreal_fire_trends.py, third_pole_trends.py): one-shot runs writing trend_results.csv, monthly_trends.csv, and three publication-quality PNGs per region.

BENEFITS

- Statistically honest. Environmental series are spiky, autocorrelated, and seasonal. Mann-Kendall + Hamed-Rao + Seasonal MK handle all three; a naive t-test would over-report significance.

- Multiple-comparison safe. Running dozens of tests inflates false positives. BH-FDR across the full test family keeps significant verdicts trustworthy.

- Spike-proof. Wildfire, methane, and black-carbon series are dominated by a few extreme years. The drop-extreme-year check exposes trends that depend on one spike year.

- Truncated-data tolerant. CO2 ends 2022-02 and methane ends 2014-08. The app renders what's available and clearly labels what couldn't be tested - no crashes.

- Readable by non-specialists. Every plot has a plain-English caption; every result is summarised in one sentence with slope, CI, and significance.

- Reproducible by design. Every CSV carries a URL to regenerate the exact series from Giovanni. The CLI writes a full audit trail (trend_results.csv) with every input, slope, CI, p-value, and FDR-adjusted p-value.

- Consistent everywhere. Dashboard, globe, and CLIs share identical formulas - numbers never disagree between interfaces.

INTENDED IMPACT

- For the NASA challenge: complete satisfaction of all four objectives (variables identified, region acquired, time series visualised, trend statistically tested and rate reported) with additional rigour (autocorrelation correction, FDR, robustness check, step-change detection).

- For researchers: a drop-in analysis harness for any Giovanni area-averaged download. Swap data/*.csv and the same pipeline runs.

- For public communication: plain-English verdicts usable in classrooms, newsrooms, and policy briefings where "Mann-Kendall p = 0.0021" needs to become "the trend is significant."

- For pedagogy: the Globe Explorer turns "which variables drive the Third-Pole snow trend?" into a clickable exercise rather than a paper-and-code exercise.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, SOFTWARE

Language: Python 3.9+

Data handling: pandas, NumPy

Statistics: SciPy (kendalltau, spearmanr, pearsonr, linregress, rankdata, norm)

Visualisation: Matplotlib (static PNGs), Plotly (interactive maps and correlation plots), globe.gl via streamlit.components.v1.html (3-D Earth)

Frontend: Streamlit (dashboard and Globe Explorer routing)

CLI: argparse

Network: requests (one-time fetch of Natural Earth world.geojson)

Hardware: Any laptop - no GPU, no cluster, under 200 MB RAM

Data source: NASA GIOVANNI / GES DISC - MERRA-2 (AOD, black carbon, snowcover), AIRS (methane), OCO-2 GEOS (CO2), NLDAS

HOW THE PROJECT IS CREATIVE

- Three-way parity. Most trend explorers are either a notebook or a dashboard. This project ships dashboard, CLI, and globe that all share one mathematical core - verified against the same acceptance test - so a result seen in one interface can be reproduced exactly in the other two.

- The Globe Explorer UX. A sector-by-sector drilldown where selecting a region smoothly swaps a rotating 3-D globe for a flat regional map, and the right-hand panel becomes an interactive correlation explorer with lagged Kendall tau and standardised beta written so non-statisticians can read them.

- Robustness built in, not bolted on. Drop-extreme-year checks, Pettitt step change, and FDR are first-class features, not optional extras. Environmental data is messy, so the tool expects to be surprised - and says so when it is.

- Plain-English verdicts. Every plot has a caption. Every result has one sentence. Every uncertain signal is explained, not hidden.

- Circumpolar-aware. The box-warnings logic automatically distinguishes a true regional box from a circumpolar band, so a Northern-band average is never mislabelled as a "boreal forest" trend.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Data quality. Fill values masked; implausible ranges rejected per variable; daily-to-monthly aggregation weighted by month length; truncated files explicitly flagged, not silently dropped.

- Statistical integrity. Autocorrelation inflation (Hamed-Rao), seasonal correlation (Hirsch-Slack cross-season covariance), multiple testing (BH-FDR across all variables and files - not per-file), and spike-year sensitivity (drop-extreme-year).

- Honest regional labels. Because four of five files use a circumpolar box, calling it "boreal forest" would be scientifically wrong. The tool labels it "Northern band (48-70 N, all longitudes)" - a zonal, not regional, average.

- Graceful degradation. Every step checks minimum data length and either skips cleanly or displays a clear note; no interface raises an uncaught exception on short or missing data.

- Reproducibility. Every CSV's "URL to Reproduce Results" line is displayed. The CLI writes a full audit trail. MASTER_PROMPT.md regenerates the entire codebase if it ever drifts from spec.

- Accessibility. A sidebar-expandable definitions panel explains every variable, unit, and statistic in one or two sentences so a fresh reviewer can understand the tool without prior stats background.

- Portability. Six pip packages, a laptop, and a browser are enough to run the whole stack.
